newsitem.title: UK: S&P ups Scottish Equitable fin strength to AAA.
newsitem.headline: S&P ups Scottish Equitable fin strength to AAA.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had raised Scottish Equitable Plc's financial strength rating to AAA from AA plus.
"The rating upgrade is primarily driven by the company's integral position in the AAA-rated AEGON group of companies," S&P said in statement.

S&P added that on a stand-alone basis, Scottish Equitable had demonstrated an improved level of capitalisation, strong business position, excellent expense management, and improved financial flexibility.

"Standard & Poor's regards the backing of AEGON as particularly important because it increases the company's flexibility in weathering the effects of the uncertain state of the UK life market and somewhat mitigates its dependence on pensions business and Independent Financial Adviser distribution," the statement said.
S&P said the major rating factor for the firm were as follows: -

-- Scottish Equitable is now positioned amongst the most strongly capitalized companies in the UK life market and enjoys strong support from a wealthy shareholder, a commitment that was evidenced in December 1995 by an injection of 325 million stg in new capital to fund the acquisition of the remaining 40 percent interest in the non-profit sub-fund previously owned by the company's with-profit policyholders, taking the ownership up to 100 percent in stages by the end of 1998.
This will complete the acquisition process which commenced in 1993. Standard & Poor's had expected this process to extend to the year 2000 by piecemeal capital injections.

By accelerating the process in what remain difficult UK market conditions, Standard & Poor's regards this action as a very strong expression of support and a confirms the strategic importance of Scottish Equitable as part of the AEGON group.

-- Following the capital contribution, the with profits free asset ratio was 17 percent at year end 1995, placing it among the higher rated UK life companies. Standard & Poor's expects this relative position to be maintained in the medium term by further injections of capital if required.

-- Scottish Equitable is a leading provider of pension products in the UK and, marketing primarily through IFAs, is a recognized specialist in both individual and group schemes. Standard & Poor's believes that the combination of recognized pensions expertise, an IFA focus, and outstanding capital strength have so far enabled Scottish Equitable to consolidate its position as one of the strongest companies in this market.

While well-positioned to build on this, Standard & Poor's believes the company risks being over-dependent on one sector. Sales in 1995 were only one percent down on 1994 which is commendable when compared with a decline of approximately 18 percent for the industry as a whole.
At year end 1996, APE rebounded sharply (annual premium + 10 percemnt of single premium income) increasing 28 percent compared to year end 1995.
-- Standard & Poor's considers the company's operating performance to be strong, with new business production, expense and persistency ratios noticeably better than the market average.

Although products satisfy profit-testing criteria and corporate targets, the company continues to take firm action to bring expenses down. The total expense ratio for the group was an excellent 9 percent for 1995. Standard & Poor's expects further improvement in profitability for 1996 and over the next few years.
-- Investment strategy remains conservative with a relatively low proportion of the with-profit portfolio in equity and real estate assets (50 percent at June 30, 1996).

This proportion was increased from 45 percent at the end of 1994, and is a reflection in part that the enhanced levels of capital strength permit somewhat greater investment flexibility. Nevertheless, Scottish Equitable's investment posture has not adversely impacted long term investment performance.

S&P said its expectations for the firm were as follows:- -- Capital will continue to remain strong; -- New business growth will exceed industry growth rates; -- Expenses will continue remain significantly below
